function: Joint optimization of BS precoder and RIS phase shifts maximizing weighted sum rate with complex-valued meta-learning networks on Riemannian manifolds (p. 1).
system: MU-MISO downlink: BS with 64 antennas (0.5 lambda spacing), K single-antenna users (K not given), reflecting RIS with 100 elements, direct link blocked, 28 GHz (p. 1-2, 4).
method: Complex-valued NN (200-neuron hidden layer) for phases, Euler-update NN for precoder; meta-learning with Riemannian ADAM; unsupervised loss (negative weighted sum rate), run per channel realization (p. 2-4).
data_channel: Simulated Rician fading (kappa=10) for BS-RIS and RIS-user links, path loss from 3GPP TS 36.814, same setup as [4], [12]; 100 channel realizations; no dataset (p. 3-4).
test_conditions: No training/test split described; algorithm run on each of 100 channel realizations, averaged; sweeps over power, N, M; imperfect-CSI results only in supplement (p. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: AO [15] (WMMSE + Riemannian conjugate gradient), AO initialized from GAMN as upper bound. Learned: GMML [4], GNN [21]; GAMNreal variant (p. 4).
metrics: Weighted sum rate (bps) vs transmit power, N and M; power gain in dB; epochs to converge; runtime and energy only in supplement (p. 4-5).
complexity: Order O(Ne No Ni K^2 M N), same as [4], no cubic term; runtime and energy only in supplementary Appendix A (p. 5).
openness: none: no code or data link; appendices are in supplementary material (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 3: "is assumed to follow Rician fading" and p. 4: "The path loss is set according to the 3GPP standard". Custom Rician simulator that takes only its path loss from 3GPP TS 36.814; no TR 38.901 channel, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "We also run the algorithm for 100 channel realizations and average our results." The algorithm is run afresh per realization and per sweep over power, N and M; no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 4: "Manifold Meta-Learning (GMML) method [4] and the conventional alternating optimization (AO) approach [15]", compared on weighted sum rate: "GAMN outperforms GMML by a weighted sum rate difference of 0.7 bps" and "GAMN outperforms the traditional AO baseline by 0.86 bps".
q4_support: p. 5: "the total computational complexity becomes O(Ne No Ni K 2 M N )", i.e. O(Ne No Ni K^2 M N), stated as the same as for [4] and free of cubic terms.
q5_support: p. 4: "All appendices referenced in the main text are provided in the Supplementary material." No link to code or data is given and the channels are simulated (p. 3: "we set the same channel parameters and setup as in [4] and [12]").
notes: Included as learned: the networks PL and PRL give the RIS phases and the precoder, and Algorithm 1 (p. 3) randomly initializes the weights and optimizes them by Riemannian ADAM on the negative weighted sum rate for each channel realization, with no training dataset; the reviewer may want to confirm this is not a no_learning case. Area 3. The PDF has 5 pages and the appendices A-F (training time of GNN [21], runtime and energy, imperfect CSI, scalability, learning-rate sensitivity, detailed complexity) are in a supplement that is not in this PDF, so they were not graded. The IEEE footnote on p. 1 points to supplementary material at the paper DOI; the main text describes it as the appendices, not code or data, so q5 is 0 but worth a check.
